system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: TESTAGENTdesigns a prompt template to conduct semantic analysis and abstraction of the target function

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent begins by utilizing an external retrieval toolkit to actively query context information (e.g., program entities and dependencies) related to the focal method from the knowledge graph.
env_context_strategy.note: Graph-based retrieval tools invoked autonomously by the agent.

observation_format.evidence_quote: These results are formatted into a JSON format report, which serves as feedback for the reviewer agent

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: we equip TESTAGENTwith a set of tool APIs that can be invoked dynamically in an on-demand and adaptive man- ner
tool_call_format.note: Paper does not state the call syntax; tool APIs assumed function-call style.

tool_count.note: Counted Table I: 4 graph manipulation + 7 information retrieval + 5 runtime interaction = 16.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: update_test_casesUpdates test cases and test reports for the corresponding focal method.
edit_primitive.note: Edits are whole generated test case files/entries; no diff or line-range primitive described.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: we build a set of tool APIs (e.g., con- text retrieval and test validation) that agents can invoke au- tonomously
tool_schema_source.note: Tools described with hand-written descriptions in Table I; no schema generator reported.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: we design a set of tools to facilitate efficient interaction between agents and external resources.
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mentioned anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the agent operates through a series of adaptive states based on the “observe-think-act” cognitive decision-making paradigm
loop_primitives.note: Generate-validate-repair loop plus requirement planning stage.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Each test requirement point specifies the testing intention, input type, and expected output behavior.
planning_granularity.note: test_point.json requirement objects stored and reused.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: we design three dedicated agents (i.e., requirement planner, test generator, and reviewer) to simulate this development practice. Each agent is responsible for a specific stage of the process

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: provides actionable suggestions that are iteratively fed back to the above two agents to guide their subsequent behaviors

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: All intermediate agent reasoning steps are displayed in an interactive panel, where developers can preview, edit, or insert test cases as needed.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: this agent operates in two internal states:function summaryandtest requirement.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: further serves as a persistent store for dynamically generated testing artifacts (e.g., function summaries, test reports, and root-cause analyses)
long_term_memory.note: Neo4J knowledge graph persists artifacts across focal methods; closest value is episodic_db.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: The graph is constructed once per project and shared across all focal methods, and is incrementally maintained by the graph manipulation tools as testing proceeds.
state_persistence.note: Persistent graph state; no explicit resume path described.

self_verification.evidence_quote: the agent invokes external tools for syntax checking, compilation, and sandboxed execution
self_verification.note: Reviewer agent evaluates; three-LLM voting confirms defects.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: If the retry budget is exhausted before a compilable test is produced for a highly complex focal method, the agent records the last attempt as a best-effort result

rollback.evidence_quote: its related graph entries are deleted (i.e., calling delete_test_casestool in Table I)
rollback.note: Discard deletes generated tests; no repo rollback/snapshot mechanism reported.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: the agent is explicitly queried about context sufficiency after 30 interaction turns, and test generation is enforced after 40 turns, within the maximum recursion depth
termination_condition.note: Max recursion depth 50; generation terminates when test passes or defect confirmed.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: To prevent long contexts, we select only the top-5 test requirements generated by the planner agent for subsequent processing, and set the maximum recursion depth to 50.

timeouts.evidence_quote: EvoSuite is run with a search budget of 300 seconds per class.
timeouts.note: Time budget stated only for the EvoSuite baseline; no harness timeout for TestAgent reported.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: iteratively refines them based on execution feedback in a sandbox environment

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Given a focal method under test and its project repository
filesystem_access.note: Access scoped to the project under test.

network_policy.evidence_quote: accessed via API or deployed on independent hardware

permission_model.evidence_quote: All three types of tools are exposed to every agent, which autonomously selects the appropriate tool according to its current state.

tracing.evidence_quote: A JSON report is also provided, detailing each test case, its target requirement, coverage, and mutation performance, facilitating transparent inspection and CI integration.

replayability.evidence_quote: Our results are obtained from a single run of each approach due to the substantial mone- tary and time costs, and the inherent randomness of LLMs may introduce variance

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We implement TESTAGENTas a VSCode unit generation plugin to support practical adoption and developer interaction
eval_hooks.note: No evaluation runner shipped; benchmarks run externally.

guardrails.evidence_quote: The correctness of generated test cases is verified via an automated pipeline, in which the agent invokes external tools for syntax checking, compilation, and sandboxed execution.
guardrails.note: Validation gates acceptance of generated tests; no safety guardrails described.

target_domain.evidence_quote: TESTAGENT, an LLM-based test generation approach

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: This confirms TESTAGENT’s model-agnostic design and its robustness in varied deploy- ment scenarios.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv v1 date; no release tags.
